text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Richard Holbrooke, appointed the U.S. envoy on the Cyprus dispute on Wednesday, will assemble a team to deal with the issue at the U.S. State Department.
- New survey reveals regional schools in rural areas are better for students rather than schools serving just one community.
- A parliamentary vote to extend the working contracts of government doctors and nurses for another six months averts a looming crisis in the island's hospitals.
- The appointment of Richard Holbrooke as Washington's emissary on the Cyprus problem gets a broad welcome in Cyprus.
- By extending the temporary contracts of doctors and nurses in hospitals, parliament attempts a patchwork solution to the problems in the health sector caused by lack of government programming.
- Turkish warplanes violated Cyprus's airspace again on Thursday.
- Richard Holbrooke is working on a strategy for Cyprus which may start yielding results in months, if not years.
- Dangerous gas cylinders are on the market.

- A government board cancels its invitation for tender for the maintenance of the SCOOT software system in traffic lights because the only bid submitted was too high and made by the suppliers of the product.

- The U.S. expects rapid developments on the Cyprus dispute in 1998, believing that the current political instability in Turkey, the upcoming presidential elections in Cyprus and the fact that no progress was achieved in the U.N. proximity talks between the Turkish and Greek Cypriot sides are impediments.
- Shopkeepers plan three-hour strike on Wednesday in protest at new extended opening hours for shops in tourist-designated areas.
